subject: Don't over-allocate XXH32/XXH64, don't hardcode
perf_evidence: "Don't over-allocate XXH32/XXH64 ... XXH32_state_t and XXH64_state_t are no longer overaligned": XXH32/XXH64_createState use plain malloc instead of the 64-byte-aligning over-allocating XXH_malloc (memory/allocation cost).
change_summary: xxhash.h: XXH_malloc/XXH_free become plain malloc/free; the aligning allocator is renamed XXH_alignedMalloc/XXH_alignedFree (generic power-of-2 alignment) in xxh3.h and used only by XXH3_createState/freeState.

units.name: XXH32_createState/freeState (create, reset(seed), digest, free)
units.evidence: fwd correct; bwd counterexample: old (as tgt) malloc returns null -> returns 0, new returns the hash: clang elides the new malloc/free pair entirely (heap-to-nothing), the old over-allocating version keeps malloc (may fail)

units.name: XXH64_createState/freeState (create, reset(seed), digest, free; and create+free only)
units.evidence: fwd correct, bwd incorrect (same allocation-failure counterexample); create+free-only target r_api_t4: fwd correct, bwd incorrect

units.name: XXH3_createState/freeState (XXH_malloc -> XXH_alignedMalloc rename/generalisation)
units.evidence: create+free target: Alive2 fwd+bwd correct (both keep malloc/free)

units.name: heap states with data: XXH32 20 B, XXH64 40 B, XXH3 100 B (create, reset, update, digest, free)
units.evidence: SMT timeouts (60 s) in both directions for r_api_t1/t2/t3

notes: Allocation-only change. Alive2 models malloc as possibly returning NULL. For the checked empty-input XXH32/XXH64 paths, the new code refines the old: clang removes the new malloc/free pair, while the old over-allocating version retains a malloc that may fail. This is a proven one-way result for those units only. Data-bearing API paths timed out in both directions, so the commit-level verdict is UNKNOWN. Harness wrap_api.c (identical for old/new): heap state via XXH*_createState, return 0 if NULL. Runner c/xxHash/4f43b71/xx_alive_d.py with Alive2 malloc/free modeling.
